- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.65) — reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.25) — increase forecast to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Overshoot after recent spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Lagged price movements often overcorrect — adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead by subtracting 0.5–1.5% of recent trend magnitude.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and history shows volatility, reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 3+ consecutive negative sentiment days — cap at 1–2% above recent low.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.65–1.56) and price is falling, anticipate reversal — forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
